BLOCKER: `product-forge/conftest.py` assigns `os.environ["PF_BACKLOG_DB"] = "off"` at import for the whole suite, overriding `backlog-db.yml`'s `PF_BACKLOG_DB: "on"`: the DB-mode job actually runs file mode, so AC-2's "a DB-mode integration job runs with on" is not delivered (and the file is not in `affected_files`).

`0023_backlog_global_id_guard` exempts legacy rows on both sides: the partial unique index and the trigger both filter `legacy_duplicate=false`, so a new row may reuse an `id` held by a `legacy_duplicate=true` row in another tenant — "no new duplicate is accepted" is not enforced at the DB.
MAJOR: Authority default diverges: `_db_for`/`store_item_to_db` default missing `project`/`scope` to `"product_forge"` (DB), but `db_authority_enabled` used by `id_allocator` defaults to `""` (not allowlisted) — an unattributed call gets DB items and Git ID allocation, violating "one allowlist key" and "no Git fallback".

`delete()` resolves authority via `str(project or scope or "")` while `_save_item`/`store_item_to_db` default to `"product_forge"`; an item with neither field is written to the DB tenant but deleted through the file path, leaving orphan DB rows.

`backlog_db_export.py` unlinks prunable projections *before* writing replacements; an interrupted rollback export leaves the file authority incomplete exactly when it is the recovery source — prune after successful writes.
`go/edpdata.requireTenant` scans `current_setting('app.tenant_id', true)` into a `string`; a genuinely unset GUC returns NULL → scan error (500), not `ErrTenantContext` (503) as FR-4 declares.
`0023` runs `UPDATE backlog_items` plus a non-concurrent `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX` on the shared table in one transaction, with no preflight/backup gate (unlike 0021) and only `statement_timeout='60s'`.
No test covers `BACKLOG_DB_SCOPES_EMPTY` (FR-1 edge case / config contract) nor the delete-path fail-closed behaviour in `on` mode, despite FR-1/FR-4 acceptance text.

`[OUT_OF_SCOPE]` `architect_review.py` narrows `EXCLUDE` so `engineering/**` (except reviews/trails/learnings) and `data/backlog/**` (except open/closed/history) now enter every review diff — design packs, evidence and item JSON inflate and contaminate all future reviews.
MINOR: AC-1/AC-4/AC-5 evidence `db-mode-tests.txt` and `failclosed-rollback-tests.txt` are committed as binary, so the cited test output is not reviewable.
`engineering/evidence/BI-PF-1531/authority-db-test.txt` records `ok productforge/edpsvc (cached)` — a cached Go run is not evidence of a fresh migration+DB run.
`backlog_db_backfill.py` docstring still advertises `PF_API_TOKEN` while the code requires `PF_EDP_TOKEN`/`PF_ADMIN_TOKEN` — the exact docs/code drift this item exists to remove.
`docs/BACKLOG-DB-SSOT.md` leaves an orphaned 1..6 list under **Activate** after the `## Rollback` heading removal, duplicating and contradicting `## Rollback / reconcile`.

Fail-closed taxonomy is not uniform: only `_load_all_from_db` maps transport failures to `BACKLOG_DB_UNAVAILABLE`; on-mode write/delete paths surface raw `urllib` errors despite the design's `failure_behavior` claim.
`0022` runs `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` under `statement_timeout='60s'` with no sizing/retry note; on a large `traceability` it aborts and the deploy retries blindly.
`docs/PF-DESIGN-DELIVERY-CONTRACT.md` and `functional_spec.open_questions` contain `?` mojibake where `→`/`—` belong; the encoding gate does not flag them.
NIT: Tests obfuscate literals (`"." + "json"`, `"fac" + "tory"`, `"backlog-" + "db" + _Y`) to dodge content gates, hiding intent from readers.
`config/store-registry.json` adds `functional-spec.json`/`spec-pack.json` to an ignore-style list, which will mask future drift in those files.
`backlog_db_export.py` injects `project` into `data` after id validation for non-`product_forge` tenants, so the written file differs from the DB row parity later compares.
`docs/GLOSSARY.md` appends `PF_BACKLOG_DB` after the document's closing "One line" statement.
SUMMARY: Direction is right and much of the cutover is genuinely implemented (scoped allowlist, tenant-bound Go store, preflight, export/prune guards, fail-closed reads), but two integrity blockers remain: the DB-mode CI job is neutralised by the new root conftest, and 0023 does not enforce global-ID uniqueness for new rows.
Highest residual risk: item vs ID authority resolve different defaults, so the "single allowlist, no Git fallback" invariant can silently split.

Secondary risks: rollback export can destroy the file authority before rewriting it, tenant context is a 500 rather than the declared 503 when the GUC is truly unset, and 0023 deploys without the 0021-style preflight/backup discipline.
